aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:861.title: Ontario Reign - Team Photographer (Part-Time)
aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:861.description: Company Information For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer. Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations. If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer! JOB DESCRIPTION: The Ontario Reign part-time Team Photographer is responsible for assisting the team with a variety of projects including coverage of events and gameday activities, promotional photo initiatives, photo editing, digital asset management, and assist with gameday workflow. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Photograph pregame, in-game, and postgame activities as well as game action and theme night needs for Reign home games. Upload images from games to Flickr. Organize, manage and process internal and external photography and imaging requests. Assist with coverage of corporate partnership events, community events, and other events as needed and assigned Edit photos to be used across Reign digital platforms and creative assets Collaborate with creative, social, and video teams for assigned projects Other duties as assigned SPECIFIC JOB KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND ABILITY: The Team Photographer must possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities and be able to explain and demonstrate that he or she can perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation, using some other combination of skill and abilities: Strong personal and communication skills including the ability to interact with both athletes and executives. Must have a strong knowledge of DSLR cameras and ancillary equipment. Flexible schedule to allow commitment to a minimum of 90% of Ontario Reign home games during the 2026-27 season, including some weekends, evenings, and some holidays to meet game/event needs Ability to stand in one spot for 45 minutes. Possess a strong work ethic and positive attitude Must have a strong knowledge of hockey REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Education: High School Diploma or its equivalency (BA/BS Degree Preferred) Experience: A minimum of 2-4 years of related experience of professional photography experience, specializing in sports and entertainment. Payscale: $20/hr Bonus: This position is not eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements. Benefits Part-time: This position may be eligible for benefits (ACA qualification). AEG may require an employee to perform duties outside their normal description. AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants, and we comply with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws in making hiring and employee decisions. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, marital status, disability, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected status recognized by applicable federal, state or local law. astraservicespartners-astraservicespartn.title: Operating Associate
astraservicespartners-astraservicespartn.description: Operating Associate — Continuous Improvement Department Orion Group | Two-year operator development program | Boulder, CO home base with travel across U.S. / territories / Canada About Orion Orion exists to redefine what a career in the service trades looks like. We are a network of operating companies across the United States, U.S. territories, and Canada, working to become the gold standard for people in our industry. We win through people leadership, technical superiority, and business excellence. We are the employer-of-choice for top talent in our industry, and we invest in development to create career opportunities that don't exist anywhere else in the service trades. About the Operating Associate Program The Operating Associate role is a two-year apprenticeship designed to develop high-potential early-career talent into future leaders of Orion. You will learn the disciplines of Continuous Improvement, the operational problem-solving methodology used by world-class operating businesses, while building toward placement into an Orion Operating Company in a leadership role such as Director, Operations Manager, or other mid-level operating position, with a clear path to continue advancing toward more senior operating leadership over time. This is not a traditional analyst program. You will spend the majority of your time traveling to Astra Operating Companies, learning their businesses from the inside, contributing to real operational improvement work, and developing the judgment to eventually lead one of these companies yourself. What you'll do • Travel to Orion Operating Companies . Roughly 50–70% of your time will be spent on-site at our operating companies across the U.S., territories, and Canada. You will work alongside their teams, observe their operations, and contribute to Continuous Improvement work in service of their business outcomes. • Learn the businesses we serve . You'll spend deliberate time in different parts of each operating company, dispatch, operations, sales, finance, ride-alongs with technicians, building real understanding of how service-trades businesses succeed and where they get stuck. • Apprentice in Continuous Improvement. You'll learn the A3 problem-solving method from senior senseis, contribute to real CI engagements at operating companies, and progressively take on more of the coaching work yourself as your capability develops. • Build business literacy. You'll learn to read a P&L, understand operational KPIs, see how leadership decisions flow through to results, and develop the judgment of an operator. Coursework includes Orion University, the LAUNCH program for operational excellence, and in-person training at the University of Tennessee. • Develop through structured gates. You will pass through six structured capability assessments across the two years, quarterly in Year 1, semi-annually in Year 2, each one a real evaluation of your readiness for the next stage of development. What you'll learn • How to solve operational problems using proven Continuous Improvement methods, A3 thinking, Kaizen, Lean, Kanban, and structured problem-solving disciplines. • How service-trades businesses actually work, the economics, the operations, the people, the leadership choices that separate good from great. • How to coach teams through structured problem-solving and build their capability rather than solve their problems for them. • How to read a business through an operator's eyes: P&L, KPIs, organizational health, customer dynamics, talent. • How to lead through influence and partnership rather than authority, the central skill of operating leadership. Who we're looking for Required : • Bachelor's degree by your start date. • Willingness to be based in Boulder, CO, with travel 50–70% of your working time across the U.S., territories, and Canada in Year 1. • Willingness to relocate within 2–3 years for placement at an Orion Operating Company. • U.S. work authorization. beaconsoftware-beaconsoftware:ashbyhq:81.title: Technical Project Manager, Integrations
beaconsoftware-beaconsoftware:ashbyhq:81.description: THE ROLE Beacon acquires vertical market software companies and brings them onto a common operating standard. Integration is the function that runs the window between close and steady state, coordinating IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR so that a newly acquired company lands cleanly rather than by improvisation. You will run that window. Each integration is a fixed, fast-moving program with a defined start and a defined handoff, and you will be the person holding the plan, the cadence, and the escalations across every function involved. This is a hands-on role. You will drive the plan and you will do work inside it. WHAT YOU'LL DO Run integrations from close to handoff. Own the integration plan for each acquisition: scope, sequencing, owners, and dates across every function. Drive the recurring cadence, keep the plan current, and land the handoff on time. Be the coordination point for the acquired company. Work directly with the GM and their team through their first weeks inside Beacon. Translate between how they operate today and how Beacon operates, and make sure nothing lands on them twice or not at all. Move companies onto the Beacon standard. Identity, devices, security baselines, and core business systems. You will partner with IT, Security, and the systems owners to sequence the migrations and to unblock them when they stall. Hold the line on status. Report progress honestly to leadership, including the parts that are behind. Escalate early and with a recommendation attached rather than late and with a surprise. Run and sharpen the playbook. Each integration should be faster and cleaner than the last. Find the steps that keep breaking, fix them in the playbook, and make the improvement stick across the next one. REQUIRED - 5+ years in project or program management, running cross-functional programs end to end - Experience coordinating across IT, Finance, GTM, Legal, and HR, or an equivalent set of functions with competing priorities - Comfort with technical systems: identity, device management, and core SaaS platforms. You do not need to configure them, but you need to follow the work and ask sharp questions - Experience building process, templates, and structure where none existed - Strong written communication. Much of this job is a clear status update landing in the right inbox at the right time - A bias for action. You would rather move something forward than perfect the plan - The agility to adapt when a program changes shape mid-stream, and the confidence to get hands-on when it needs you NICE TO HAVE - Post-close M&A integration experience, in-house or in advisory - Exposure to IAM, MDM, or SSO rollouts - Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or SOX ITGC programs - Automation experience - A habit of spotting the smarter way to do something and then doing it Our Values at Beacon Software - Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time. - Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant. - Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected. - Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth. jobgether-jobgether:lever:f491ebd5-ae01-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. This role offers the opportunity to strengthen cybersecurity operations by engineering reliable, scalable security data pipelines across cloud and on-premises environments. You will work with high volumes of security telemetry and help ensure critical data is available for threat detection, incident response, compliance, and cyber risk visibility. You’ll collaborate with application, infrastructure, security, governance, and vendor teams to onboard and optimize diverse data sources.
